article.title: Why Revenue Growth Can Hide Customer Concentration Risk
article.why: 把營收成長與客戶集中風險拆開，避免只看 headline growth。
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

paragraphs.en:
A company can report strong revenue growth and still become more fragile. One common reason is customer concentration: a large share of sales may come from only a few clients. When those clients expand their purchases, total revenue rises quickly. The headline looks positive, but the business may also become more dependent on decisions made by a small number of customers.

Imagine a software company with one hundred customers. Last year, its largest client represented 12 percent of revenue. This year, that client doubled its spending and now represents 24 percent. Total revenue may have grown impressively, but losing that single account would now create a much larger shock. The same logic applies when the top five customers together become a larger share of sales.

This is why managers should look beyond total growth. A useful first measure is the revenue share of the largest customer, the top five, and the top ten. Another is the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index, or HHI, which summarizes concentration by squaring each customer's revenue share and adding the results. You do not need the index in every meeting, but the idea is useful: two companies with the same revenue can have very different risk if one depends on a few buyers.

Concentration is not always bad. Large customers can be valuable because they provide predictable volume, strong references, and opportunities to sell additional products. Serving a major client can also help a company build capabilities that later attract other customers. The problem appears when dependence grows faster than the company's ability to manage it.

Contract structure matters too. A customer representing 20 percent of revenue under a three-year contract with committed minimum purchases is different from a customer representing 20 percent under a monthly agreement that can be canceled easily. Profitability also matters. A large client may generate high revenue but demand discounts, custom features, and dedicated support. In that case, concentration in revenue may understate concentration in operational effort.

Good analysis therefore combines several questions. How much revenue comes from the largest customers? How quickly is that share changing? Are contracts long or short? Are renewal dates clustered? Does one customer influence product priorities? Would losing a major account create unused staff or infrastructure? These questions turn a simple concentration ratio into a practical risk assessment.

Management can respond in several ways. It can diversify by acquiring smaller customers, enter new segments, negotiate longer commitments, or avoid building systems that only one client can use. It can also run scenario analysis: if the largest account disappeared tomorrow, how much revenue, gross profit, and cash flow would be lost, and how quickly could costs adjust?

The key lesson is that growth and resilience are different dimensions. Revenue growth tells you that the business is selling more. Customer concentration tells you how widely that success is distributed. A company can improve on one dimension while weakening on the other. Strong reporting should show both, because the most dangerous dependency can sometimes hide inside the best-looking growth number.

For investors or internal planners, the trend is often more informative than a single threshold. A top customer at 18 percent may be manageable if its share is falling as the rest of the business expands. The same 18 percent may deserve attention if it rose from 8 percent in one year. Direction, contract quality, and replacement difficulty give the percentage its meaning.
paragraphs.zh: 公司可能一邊高速成長、一邊變得更脆弱，原因之一就是客戶集中度上升。最大客戶或前五大客戶占比變高時，營收 headline 很漂亮，但單一客戶流失的衝擊也同步放大。集中本身不一定不好，大客戶能帶來穩定量體、案例與追加銷售；真正要看的是占比趨勢、契約長度、最低採購承諾、客製支援負擔，以及失去該客戶後成本能否快速調整。成長與韌性是兩個不同維度，好的報告應同時呈現。
paragraphs.ja: 売上成長が強くても、少数顧客への依存が高まれば事業は脆弱になり得ます。最大顧客・上位5社の構成比だけでなく、その変化方向、契約期間、最低購入保証、個別開発や専任支援の負荷まで確認する必要があります。大口顧客は価値もありますが、成長とレジリエンスは別の軸なので、両方を同時に評価することが重要です。

quiz.question: Why can strong growth still increase risk?
quiz.answer: Because growth may be driven by a small number of customers, increasing dependency.

quiz.question: What should be checked besides customer share?
quiz.answer: Contract quality, profitability, renewal timing, operational effort, and replacement difficulty.
